row.Finding description: Following myelin challenge, E3 microglia significantly acidified their lysosomes whereas E4 microglia showed no significant further acidification and a nonsignificant pH increase, without a reported genotype-by-treatment interaction test.
row.Finding quote: Following treatment with myelin, E3 microglia significantly acidified their lysosomes (Figure S3). Interestingly, a similar decrease in lysosomal pH was observed in E4 microglia relative to E3 microglia at baseline. As lysosome function is optimal at lower pH, these effects may reflect activation of the lysosomal degradation machinery to cope with the increased burden of internalized debris following myelin challenge in E3 microglia, or in E4 vs E3 microglia even before myelin challenge. E4 microglia did not exhibit further acidification following myelin challenge but rather a slight (albeit not significant) increase of their lysosomal pH (Figure S3).
row.Finding summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no significant further lysosomal acidification after myelin challenge)
row.Experimental system: Primary microglia from pooled P1–3 forebrains of homozygous human APOE3 or APOE4 targeted-replacement mice, C57BL/6 background; approximately four-week culture; untreated cells compared with cells exposed to myelin for three hours and assessed at 24 hours; lysosomal pH measured using LysoSensor and flow cytometry.
